Galeas Per Montes translates to Galleys For/To Mountains. It's a pretty interesting story...

November 1438 to April 1439. A naval battle occurred between Venice and Milan, who were competing for dominance of Lake Garda which geographically lies between them. The Venetians transported their warships over land and around mountains to reach the north end of the lake. The idea involved something like 5 big warships (including 2 galley ships), 25 smaller ships, 2000 soldiers, and some 600 cattle. Logs were used to roll the ships over land with cattle pulling them. A fierce battle was waged. Venice and Milan ended up splitting up control of the Eastern and Western banks of the lake, but the lake eventually did completely go to Venetian control sometime before or during Jacopo Tintoretto's lifetime. Jacopo Tintoretto was a court painter and painted portraits of the Doge of Venice. His son, Domenico, also worked with him. Galeas Per Montes is attributed to Jacopo, although Domenico is thought to have worked on it as well. This painting resides in the Palazzo Dulcale (the Doge's Palace) in Venice, along with other paintings depicting Venice's history.
